profile.headline: Software Engineer Sr | Ex Mission Operations | Interested in Remote Aerospace/Software Roles
profile.summary:
Hello all! I am an Aerospace Engineering graduate from The University of Texas at Austin. Although my interests are many I am truly eager to learn anything and everything. The projects and experiences I have held thus far have not only prepared me for the future but also given me a greater appreciation for engineering, especially software developers. 

Please feel free to reach out. I am more than happy to answer questions, talk shop, or just chat!

positions.title: Systems Engineer Sr
positions.description:
In addition to my prior roles I...

Analyze Cameo modeled functional and logical system architectures to develop external customer friendly reports via the Report Wizard Tool (which executes Velocity Template Language (VTL) scripts)

Develop VTL scripts to automate and customize report generation that accurately reflects the system design as it constantly iterates

Execute rapid report generation to deliver technical materials required for PDR and CDR events, and to identify design gaps or inconsistencies

Improved development time for report generation from weeks into minutes by converting our tactics from manual generation to automation via scripts

positions.title: Systems Engineer
positions.description:
Analyzed customer SRDs to develop system requirements and design

Used Cameo and SysML principles to model the functional and logical architecture of the system

positions.insights: Skills: Cross-functional Coordination · Product Life Cycle · Agile Methodologies · Mission Operations · Systems Engineering

positions.title: Undergraduate Research Assistant
positions.locationName: UT Department of Aerospace Engineering and Engineering Mechanics
positions.description:
As of Fall 2019, I joined the program Grads Linked with Undergrads (GLUE) and began my work alongside Ph.D. student Arjun Ram. Under the supervision of Dr. Maruthi Akella in the GNC Lab I worked on one of Arjun's personal projects to learn about swarm aerial robotics. Future work includes improvements on the path planning and collision avoidance demonstration at Lockheed Martin.

Roles/Skills:
▪ Investigate and understand heterogeneous robot coordination and planning
▪ Develop methods of coordination between robots from a path planning perspective
▪ Test algorithms on a ROS simulation and implement methods with a swarm of small rovers

company.name: Cockrell School of Engineering, The University of Texas at Austin

positions.title: Advisory Board, Chief Engineer
positions.locationName: UT Department of Aerospace Engineering and Engineering Mechanics
positions.description:
Mission:
Provide interdisciplinary students with the skills to become competent engineers. Design a fully composite UAV to perform autonomous flight, obstacle avoidance, image recognition, and payload delivery of a UGV at the AUVSI international competition.

Advisory Board: 2019-2020
▪ Participate in design reviews to analyze and critique the design of aircraft components 
▪ Provide expertise concerning composite manufacturing and CAD models
▪ Extend technical and non-technical guidance to future teams

Chief Engineer: 2017-2019
▪ Employed system engineering tactics to manage and delegate tasks to all hardware teams: Design, Electronics, Ground Station, Internal Systems, Structures
▪ Led a three-week interdisciplinary engineering camp to mentor and transform entry-level students into competent engineers
▪ Utilized Solidworks, OpenVSP, and Raymer’s approach to oversee the design of a custom composite fixed wing UAV for the AUVSI 2019 competition
▪ Led and developed experimental fiberglass and Kevlar composite manufacturing to improve aerodynamic efficiency
▪ Co-authored the technical paper detailing the inter-workings of the UAV and its design rationale

positions.title: Aerial Robotic Visualization Intern
positions.description:
▪ Utilized NASA’s core Flight System (cFS), a reusable software platform which coordinates missions for UAS
▪ Integrated NASA’s ICAROUS and Emergent’s DASHER cFS apps to achieve safe autonomy for multiple UAVs
▪ Performed virtualization using Linux to implement and test flight controls onboard octo-quad copters in a Software in the Loop (SITL) and Hardware in the Loop (HITL) environment
▪ Participated in daily scrums, assigned tasks for other interns using JIRA, and wrote documentation using Confluence

projects.title: Low Speed Aerodynamics Final Lab Project
projects.description: In order to conduct the "Experimental Evaluation of Leading Edge Tubercles on a NACA 4412" I created two composite airfoils, one with a straight leading edge and the other with a tubercled leading edge. The modified leading edge achieved bio-mimicry from a whale fin, and allowed us to investigate its aerodynamic effects within the water tunnel. We utilized Laser Doppler Anemometry (LDA) to measure the velocity profile, and dye injection ports protruding from the leading edge for flow visualization. Using NACA 4412 foam cores, glass bubbles, cabosil , fiberglass, bondo, dye injection pipes, and steel pipes, I was able to create both wings in two weeks.

projects.title: Longhorn Rocketry Association Certification Team
projects.description:
▪ Achieved L1 certification from Tripoli
▪ Designed and manufactured a fully composite 6 ft Rocket to launch at a height of 1,000 ft
▪ Introduced to iterative composite manufacturing, machining instruments, and rocket components
